references.text: Luke specifies that the trial took place when it became day, in contrast to Matthew and Mark who describe a nighttime trial. See the parallels in [ref:Matt 27:1|Matthew 27:1], where it states they made their decision "when it was morning".
[ref:Matt 26:57|Matthew 26:57] describes how Jesus was brought to the high priest, where the scribes and elders were gathered – a parallel account of Jesus' trial before the Council.
[ref:Mark 14:53|Mark 14:53] is Mark's parallel account that Jesus was brought to the high priest, and that all the chief priests, the elders, and the scribes came together.

[ref:Mark 15:1|Mark 15:1] tells us that the chief priests, the elders, the scribes, and the whole Council held a consultation early in the morning – this agrees with Luke's time reference "when it was day".
[ref:Joh 18:24|John 18:24] mentions that Jesus was sent bound to the high priest Caiaphas, which is John's version of the trial before the Jewish leaders.

The expression "the council of elders" (τὸ πρεσβυτέριον) is also used in [ref:Apg 22:5|Acts 22:5], where Paul refers to the same governing body – the "council of elders" – as a witness to his past as a persecutor.
[ref:Luk 22:54|Luke 22:54] describes what preceded, that Jesus was brought to the high priest's house, and forms the immediate context for the trial that takes place in verse 66.

[ref:Sal 2:2|Psalm 2:2] prophesies that "the kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together against the Lord and his anointed" – a prophetic background to the Council's gathering against Jesus, the Messiah.

[ref:Apg 4:26-27|Acts 4:26-27] quotes Psalm 2 and applies it directly to Herod and Pontius Pilate, who gathered with the Gentiles and the peoples of Israel against Jesus – the early church's interpretation of the Council's actions.

[ref:Jes 50:6|Isaiah 50:6] describes the Lord's servant who gives his back to those who strike him, forming a prophetic background for the mistreatment Jesus endured in connection with the trial before the Council.
